tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Sends a single (transactional) email to one or more addresses. The sender must belong to a verified domain of the workspace — call get_account to see which ones. An address suppressed for a bounce, a complaint or by hand fails the entire call, with its reason. An unsubscribed address still gets an i

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Returns the workspace this key grants access to, its scopes, plan, remaining emails this month (queued sends included), when the counter resets, billing status, member and domain limits, sending domains (verified or not) and registered senders. Call this FIRST: it tells you which address to send fro

tools.name: list_subscribers
tools.description: Lists the workspace's subscribers, page by page. Use `cursor` with the `next_cursor` value from the response to get the next page. `status` filters on subscribed, pending, unsubscribed, bounced, or complained.

tools.name: add_subscriber
tools.description: Adds or updates a subscriber. By default the person enters as PENDING and receives a confirmation email: that is double opt-in, and it protects the workspace's sending reputation. `double_opt_in: false` subscribes directly and must only be used when consent was already collected elsewhere — never on

tools.name: remove_subscriber
tools.description: Unsubscribes an address and adds it to the workspace's suppression list: no more campaigns, automations, or sends carrying `unsubscribe_url`. The record is not deleted — that is what prevents the address from coming back on the next file import. This action cannot be reversed via the API: only the p

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: The workspace's tags, with how many subscribers carry each one (`subscribers`) and, among them, the active ones (`subscribed`). Read this before tagging: reuse an existing name rather than creating a near-duplicate.

tools.name: tag_subscriber
tools.description: Adds (`add`) and removes (`remove`) tags on ONE existing subscriber, and nothing else: no subscription, no confirmation email, no status touched. Prefer it to add_subscriber for changing tags: add_subscriber is a subscription and sends the confirmation again to a pending person. An unknown address i

tools.name: erase_subscriber
tools.description: Erases a person from the workspace at THEIR request (right to erasure): record, name, fields, proof of consent, tags. Statistics of campaigns already sent do not move; the suppression list is not touched. To stop someone receiving anything, use remove_subscriber — not this one. IRREVERSIBLE: only us

tools.name: list_suppression
tools.description: Suppressed addresses, with their reason: bounced, complained or manually suppressed (nothing goes to them), or unsubscribed (no more campaigns, automations, or sends carrying `unsubscribe_url`, but an individual email still reaches them). The `scope` field tells whether the address is suppressed for

tools.name: add_suppression
tools.description: Adds an address to the workspace's suppression list. By default (`manual`), it will receive nothing further, neither campaigns nor individual emails; with `unsubscribe`, only campaigns, automations, and sends carrying `unsubscribe_url` are refused to it. Use when someone requests no further contact

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: The workspace's campaigns, from newest to oldest, with their status: draft, scheduled, sending, or sent.

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.description: Creates a DRAFT. Nothing is sent: you then need to call send_campaign, or send it from the Mailcheer workspace. Content is written in plain text in `text` — a blank line separates paragraphs, "#" at the start of a line makes a heading. Always have the draft reviewed before sending.

tools.name: update_campaign
tools.description: Edits a DRAFT: name, subject, preheader, kind, sender, content (`text`). Nothing is sent. Prefer it to create_campaign to rework a text: otherwise the old draft stays in the list. A scheduled, sending or sent campaign cannot be edited (409).

tools.name: preview_campaign_send
tools.description: Read-only: nothing is sent. Returns exactly what send_campaign would do right now — would it go out (and if not, why), and how many people would receive it. With `to`, reports address by address who is kept and who is excluded, with the reason (unsubscribed, bounced, complained, not in the list…). I

tools.name: send_campaign
tools.description: ⚠️ IRREVERSIBLE. Locks the recipient list and triggers sending to ALL active subscribers in the workspace — or, with `to`, only to the requested addresses that are active subscribers (never an unsubscribed or suppressed address). A sent email cannot be recalled. First call preview_campaign_send with

tools.name: get_campaign_stats
tools.description: Status and figures for a campaign: recipients, sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complained. Rates are calculated on delivered messages, not on recipients. Every rate comes twice: open_rate and click_rate include bots (security gateways, preloads), human_open_rate and human_click_rate set t

tools.name: get_email
tools.description: Status of an email sent via send_email: sent, delivered, bounced, or complained. Amazon's delivery callback arrives a few seconds to a few minutes after sending — a "sent" status right after the call is normal.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "send_email" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account, add_subscriber, list_suppression, add_suppression, send_campaign, get_campaign_stats, get_email · Private data: remove_subscriber, erase_subscriber, add_suppression · Public sink: send_email, get_account, add_subscriber, tag_subscriber, list_suppression, create_campaign, preview_campaign_send, send_campaign, get_email · Destructive: send_email, remove_subscriber, tag_subscriber, preview_campaign_send.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account, add_subscriber, list_suppression, add_suppression, send_campaign, get_campaign_stats, get_email · Private data: remove_subscriber, erase_subscriber, add_suppression · Public sink: send_email, get_account, add_subscriber, tag_subscriber, list_suppression, create_campaign, preview_campaign_send, send_campaign, get_email · Destructive: send_email, remove_subscriber, tag_subscriber, preview_campaign_send

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "send_email" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
